# The upstream stack that pull-request CI installs.
#
# WHAT IT IS FOR. On a pull-request run and on a push to `main`, every job of
# ci.yml that installs the project adds `-c .github/constraints/pinned-upstream.txt`
# to its `pip install` (the `plan` job decides: its QUICK and APPROVAL runs). A
# new release of one of the packages below therefore cannot fail every open pull
# request at once, for a reason none of them can fix from its branch.
#
# WHERE A NEW RELEASE STILL SHOWS. The nightly full run on `main`, a manual
# dispatch, a push to `release/**` and the weekly `dependency drift` job install
# with no constraints and resolve the newest release of everything. A break
# upstream turns the nightly run red: on `main`, once, within a day.
# `transformers-floor` is separate and installs the exact floor in
# transformers-floor.txt on every run it is part of. Everything `.[dev]` pulls in
# that is not listed here (numpy, pydantic, mcp, bitsandbytes, pytest, ...) still
# resolves the newest on every run.
#
# WHEN TO BUMP IT.
#   * The nightly full run is green on versions newer than these. The suite is
#     known to pass on them, and a pull request should be tested on what a user
#     installs today.
#   * The nightly full run is red on a new release. The pull request that fixes
#     `main` for it bumps the pin in the same change, so that its own cells run
#     the fix on the new version.
#   * A bound in pyproject.toml moves past a pin. pip can no longer resolve the
#     cell, and tests/test_ci_pinned_upstream.py fails and names the pin.
#
# HOW.
#   python -m pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed -e ".[dev]"
# prints `Would install ...`: the newest version of every package that
# pyproject.toml admits. It downloads the wheels it resolves, so run it on
# Windows or macOS, where torch is one wheel of about 125 MB and brings no CUDA
# libraries. Copy the versions of the packages listed below, update the last
# paragraph of this header, run
#   pytest --no-cov -q tests/test_ci_pinned_upstream.py
# and open a pull request. Its own run installs under the new pins; with the
# `ci:full` label it does so on every required OS and Python and in the smoke
# jobs, before anything merges.
#
# FORMAT. One line per package, `name==version` and nothing else. The test
# refuses a range, a wildcard, a marker, a pip option, a trailing comment and a
# second line for one package. No line needs a marker today: every version
# below has a wheel for ubuntu x86_64, Windows amd64 and macOS arm64 on Python
# 3.10 to 3.12 (torch, tokenizers and safetensors checked against the PyPI file
# list; the other six are pure Python).
#
# THESE VERSIONS are what `test (ubuntu-latest, 3.12)` installed in the newest
# green push to `main` when the file was written (run 37983269245, 2026-10-09,
# commit 61e8c2bf). The green nightly run of 2026-10-12 (38239783640, same
# commit) resolved the same nine on ubuntu 3.10, Windows 3.12 and macOS 3.12 and
# in pytorch-smoke, torchao-contract and mlx-smoke.
torch==2.14.1
transformers==5.19.0
tokenizers==0.23.3
huggingface-hub==2.2.0
safetensors==0.8.0
trl==0.29.1
peft==0.21.2
accelerate==1.15.0
datasets==5.1.0
